  PROBLEM: The fingerprint gate in `_resolver_test_repair_main` runs `verify_integration_fingerprints.py "${INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_FILE}"` as an absolute check. It never captures a baseline with `--baseline-fingerprints-state` before `_resolver_sandbox_attempt` and never compares with `--compare-against-baseline` afterwards, but it still reverts on `fp_rc=1`. The conflict-resolver path in the same file does both (lines 1821-1850 / 1840, and 2207-2222 / 2210 / 3876).
  WHY: If the integration head already has fingerprint drift (for example, a clean default-branch sync removed a `must_contain` line), every repair is reverted with `outcome=repair_reverted reason=fingerprints`, whatever the model edits. Each attempt also uses up an `integration_test_repair_dispatches` slot of the `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX` budget, so the project can never be repaired. All reviewers rated this MAJOR, mapped here to high.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1458 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The inline Python renderer for `{{INTENT_FINGERPRINTS_JSON}}` cuts the fingerprint JSON at an arbitrary point at 65,536 characters and appends a non-JSON truncation note. The prompt therefore gets malformed, incomplete JSON, and the model cannot see the fingerprints past the cutoff.
  WHY: The repair model may misread the fingerprints or ignore them. It may then violate a pattern it never saw, and the full-file verifier rejects the repair, which uses up the head's one repair turn. The added test only covers the small-fingerprint case. Severity disagreement: gemini rated MAJOR (high), while minimax, luna and glm rated NIT (low), so the highest is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly declined to report it: the hard gate reads the full file, and no concrete runtime failure follows from the cap.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24490 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_dispatch_integration_test_repair` does not check that `tracking_issue="${1:-}"` is a valid numeric issue number before using it in API calls or logs.
  WHY: An unset or empty tracking issue could make API calls or log output fail or be attributed to the wrong issue. Gemini rated it NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dispute it because the identifier appears only in a log label and drives no API call.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1532-1539 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In `_resolver_test_repair_main`, the fingerprint gate runs `verify_integration_fingerprints.py "${INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_FILE}"` against the whole tree and treats `fp_rc -eq 1` as `outcome="fingerprints"`. It never records a baseline. By contrast, `_capture_fingerprints_baseline` (lines 1821-1850) uses `--baseline-fingerprints-state` and the post-run check (lines 2207-2222) uses `--compare-against-baseline`. The verifier docstring (scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py lines 49-56) says compare mode only hard-fails on regressions the resolver introduced.
  WHY: A clean default-branch sync or a sibling squash-merge can leave fingerprint drift on the head, so the verifier exits 1 whatever the model edited. Every repair is reverted with `outcome=repair_reverted reason=fingerprints`. The poller has already recorded `integration_test_repair_sha` and increased `integration_test_repair_dispatches`, so slots are wasted until `INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX` is reached. Suggested fix (about 6-8 lines): capture a baseline with `--baseline-fingerprints-state "${dir}/fp_baseline.json"` (`|| true`), compare with `--compare-against-baseline` when the file is non-empty, and fall back to the absolute check, as lines 1842-1848 do.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1532-1539 (approximately; `_resolver_test_repair_main` fingerprint check block) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The verifier runs against the absolute state of the integration head. The conflict-resolver path (lines 1821-1849 and 2207-2222) captures a baseline with `--baseline-fingerprints-state "${dir}/fp_baseline.json"` and compares with `--compare-against-baseline`. The test-repair path skips both and treats any exit 1 as a failed repair.
  WHY: A head that already violates a fingerprint (for example, after a prior default-branch sync) returns `fp_rc=1` on the first turn whatever the model edits. The repair is reverted with `outcome=repair_reverted reason=fingerprints`, a dispatch slot is still used, and the project can never get a repair until the head is rebuilt. The 16 KiB failures cap and the truncation note do not help, because the bug is on the verifier side.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1458 (inline Python renderer) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `fp=(fp[:65536]+'\n(fingerprints truncated ...)') if len(fp)>65536 else fp` cuts at character 65536 without regard to JSON structure, so the value substituted into `{{INTENT_FINGERPRINTS_JSON}}` no longer parses.
  WHY: When `merged_issue_fingerprints` is longer than 65,536 characters, a must_contain pattern after the cutoff is invisible to the model, and the full-file verifier rejects the repair. `test_test_repair_prompt_carries_the_intent_fingerprints` covers only the small case, and the truncation branch has no test.
